signatures.name: Catch-all tarpit
signatures.description: Returns a tool list for any request — including a nonsense tool or method name. A real server rejects what it does not implement; a tarpit answers everything.

signatures.name: MCP banner without a real handshake
signatures.description: Advertises MCP in its banner but never completes a real initialize + tools/list handshake.

signatures.name: Incoherent appliance banner
signatures.description: Claims to be an MCP server while also naming a network appliance (VPN, router, camera, NAS, …). Real servers do not also advertise as hardware.

signatures.name: Cross-network fingerprint reuse
signatures.description: An identical response fingerprint replicated across many IPs and three or more networks (ASNs). A genuine server is near-unique; a mass decoy is not.
